content: 1. The metabolism of disopyramide may be affected by atazanavir through its influence on the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4, potentially increasing its levels or effects. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 2. Atazanavir can increase the levels or effects of docetaxel by altering its metabolism via the CYP3A4 enzyme. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear. 3. Atazanavir may elevate the levels or effects of donepezil by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical relevance of this interaction remains uncertain. 4. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of atazanavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 5. Atazanavir can increase the levels or effects of dutasteride by altering its metabolism through CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear. 6. Atazanavir may elevate the levels or effects of efavirenz by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, efavirenz decreases atazanavir levels through an unspecified mechanism. Co-administration is possible, but dosing adjustments should follow the atazanavir monograph. 7. Atazanavir can increase the levels or effects of eplerenone by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 8. Eslicarbazepine acetate may reduce the levels or effects of atazanavir by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical relevance of this interaction is unclear. 9. Etravirine decreases atazanavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. However, co-administration of etravirine with atazanavir/ritonavir does not require dose adjustments, as the reduction in atazanavir levels is not clinically significant. 10.
